title: Agreement of Runs Under Agreeing Queries
statement: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic oracle Turing machine, let $O$ and $O'$ be languages over its symbol alphabet, and let $x$ be an input word and $w$ a finite sequence of choice bits. Suppose that for every $s<|w|$, if the run of $N$ with oracle $O$ on the first $s$ bits of $w$, starting from its initial configuration on $x$, is in the query state, then its query string belongs to $O$ if and only if it belongs to $O'$. Then for every $s\le |w|$, the configurations reached using the first $s$ bits of $w$ are equal for the two oracles.
hypotheses_covered: Two oracle languages $O,O'$ over the symbol alphabet
A finite sequence of choice bits $w$
For each $s<|w|$, being in the query state in the $O$-run implies agreement of the two languages on that run's query string
